rationale:
Closing the one substantive objection the council raised against migration 602 (bug_historian, advisory medium, corr c962abd1, APPROVED round 1). Quoting it: the picker steps route error_step TO the saving step with no durable record, so "a repeated LLM-picker failure would be invisible except by absence-of-effect".

The fail-open routing is right and is not changing: a cross-mention must never fail a tool build. What was wrong is that the emitter then recorded `no_related_pages` with an EMPTY `related_pages_source` — which is byte-identical to what a picker that ran and correctly answered "none" produces. So a picker failing on every single build was indistinguishable from a site with no topically-matching pages, and the emitter recorded the reassuring one of the two.

That is bugs_open/330's own root cause for the third time. 330 §2's confirmed defect was that ExtractActionInputs' strategy0Resolved bookkeeping stored "I tried and found nothing" and "I was never asked" identically; §12 found the same shape in the emitter's skip prose ('a suggestion may legitimately name no related pages', written for items no suggester ever saw); this is the third instance, one layer along, in the field the 602 picker writes.

The fix is available because a `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT key is written ONLY by the explicit-path arm (RFC_029 D2): if the picker step errored to error_step its output field does not exist and the key is ABSENT; if it ran it is PRESENT and holds the answer, empty or not. `ActionInputs.Has` (action_inputs.go:554, `ok && v != nil`) is exactly that distinction and already exists.

It also splits out a THIRD state nobody had noticed, and it is the one worth chasing: a picker that ran and returned something that is not a page list at all — prose, a refusal sentence, a malformed answer. That is a prompt or model fault, it was silent, and it is NOT the same event as an honest refusal. Two states would have hidden it behind the third.

plan.summary: ROUND 2. No change to the mechanism — round 1's three objections were all about EVIDENCE I did not attach, and all four checks came back clean (below). One substantive addition the round earned: the high objection's failure mode is now ENFORCED by a test rather than merely verified, because 'no Default on this key today' is not a property that stays true by itself. Also fixes the edit-list inconsistency both editquality and guardian caught: the RUNBOOK update my risks section promised is now listed as the edit it always was.

edits.rationale: The three-way split, at the only point that can see it. The requester-wins precedence above is untouched — this arm is reached only when nothing supplied pages, and its whole job is to say WHICH kind of nothing. `Has` is the load-bearing call: a marked key is written only by the explicit-path arm, so absent means the step produced no output field, which means it never ran or it errored to error_step.

Classifier separating a well-formed empty answer from an unreadable one. Arms mirror relatedPagesFromSpec deliberately: a list type IS a list, and reaching here means it was empty or all-blank, so the picker declined; a string counts only if it parses as the JSON array the prompt demands. Anything else is a model that stopped obeying the output format, which needs chasing rather than filing as an honest 'none'.

Five named constants rather than three plus an empty string, because these values are written into durable rows (agent_error_log context and every emitted item's spec) and read back by census queries — a typo or a collapsed pair is invisible until someone counts. Each carries what it MEANS, not just what it is.

Four new cases on the existing harness, which already drives the real extractor with the live optional-explicit config: never-ran, ran-and-declined (string `[]`), ran-and-returned-prose, and ran-and-returned-an-empty-array-VALUE (the same answer arriving as a Go slice rather than a string — both spellings must classify identically, since which one you get depends on how the step's output was stored). The mismatch message now prints the case's own reasoning, so a future failure explains itself.
edits.sketch:
cases: {no picker in collected} -> no_picker · {result: `[]`} -> picker_declined · {result: "Sorry, none of these pages fit."} -> picker_unusable · {result: []interface{}{}} -> picker_declined
assert: source == tc.wantSource, message carries tc.why

edits.rationale: ADDED IN ROUND 2, answering the high objection structurally instead of just answering it. ExtractActionInputs pre-fills spec.Defaults into Values before any strategy runs, so a Default on related_pages_fallback would make Has() true on the error_step route too and no_picker would never fire again — the bug would look exactly like the fix. Verified absent on both specs today; this test is what stops it arriving tomorrow. Mutation-proved by adding the exact Default the objection describes: the test fails and names the consequence.

LISTED IN ROUND 2 — editquality and guardian both caught that risks §1 promised this and the edit list did not contain it. It was in the same commit; the submission under-described its own change, which is the third submission-hygiene defect this lane has logged (stale sketch, truncated sketch, unlisted edit). Supersedes the interim llm_call_log workaround with a table of the five source values and what to DO about each, and states that a census spanning the roll must treat '' and no_picker as one bucket.
edits.sketch:
| `related_pages_source` | means |
|---|---|
| `spec` | the requester named the pages |
| `suggested` | the picker named them |
| `no_picker` | never ran — unwired, or failed to error_step |
| `picker_declined` | ran, none fit — a CORRECT answer (prompt rule 5) |
| `picker_unusable` | ran, answer unreadable — a prompt or model fault, the one worth chasing |

SELECT context->>'related_pages_source' AS src, count(*) FROM agent_error_log
 WHERE error_code LIKE 'tool_crosslink_not_emitted:%' AND occurred_at > '<roll time>' GROUP BY 1;

grounded_in: ROUND 1 HIGH OBJECTION (editquality) — could a Default make Has() true when the step never ran? CHECKED, both specs, first-hand: CreateToolComponentInputSpec.Defaults = {"category": "interactive"} (create_tool_component_action.go:60); DeployToolToSiteInputSpec.Defaults = {} (deploy_tool_action.go:63). Neither declares related_pages_fallback, and neither lists it as Deprecated (the other writer to Values). The objection's failure mode is ABSENT — and is now enforced by TestFallbackKeyHasNoDefault rather than left true by luck.

ROUND 1 (prior_art_librarian) — is the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker actually LIVE on the deployed chassis, given it was inert up to v1.0.1320? Settled EMPIRICALLY, which is stronger than a version comparison: 2 site_work_items exist carrying spec->>'related_pages_source' = 'suggested', created 2026-08-25 09:50:59Z. That value is reachable ONLY by the `?`-marked related_pages_fallback wire resolving through Strategy 0 on the live binary. The marker is live, on this key, in production. (Deployed tags today are v1.0.1336/1337, both far past the v1.0.1321 cutover.)

ROUND 1 (editquality, test-file name) — the existing test file IS platform/orchestration/actions/tool_cross_link_items_test.go, with no create_ prefix. `ls` of the package shows exactly two cross-link files: create_tool_cross_link_items.go and tool_cross_link_items_test.go. No stray duplicate is created; the edit appends to the real suite, which already contains TestRelatedPagesFromSpec, TestCrossLinkEmitDecision and TestCrossLinkCallSitePassesTheRealPageLive.

ROUND 1 (guardian, low) — does the value-space change break a reader? CHECKED: grep over Go/SQL/sh/py outside docs finds related_pages_source at exactly two sites, both WRITERS inside create_tool_cross_link_items.go (:367 skip context, :537 item spec). Live agent_definitions naming it: 0. Existing rows keep their empty string; nothing reads it but the runbook queries in this submission.

The objection being closed, verbatim from the c962abd1 round-1 council_report (bug_historian, medium): "Migration 602 routes the new picker steps' error_step directly to 'save_tool' (the happy-path continuation) with no visible logging/error-record step in between... a repeated LLM-picker failure would be invisible except by absence-of-effect."

datahelpers.ActionInputs.Has, action_inputs.go:554, returns `ok && v != nil`. A `?` marked field never meets ExtractFields and is written only by the explicit-path arm (the withoutStrict/explicitOnly block), which is what makes absence mean 'the step produced no output field'.

Mutation-proved in a git-archive-HEAD copy (verify-head-builds.sh --with, KEEP_TREE=1, mutated INSIDE the kept tree so the shared working copy never held a mutation): dropping the Has() check fails the never-ran case; an always-true classifier fails the prose case; dropping its []interface{} arm fails the empty-array case. Round 2's guard test proved the same way — adding the Default the objection describes makes it fail and name the consequence. Full package green against HEAD; go build ./platform/... clean.
plan.risks:
1. The empty-source value disappears from new rows. Nothing queries related_pages_source yet — it shipped 2026-08-24 and its only consumers are the RUNBOOK's verification queries, which I own and am updating in the same change. Existing rows keep their empty string; a census spanning the change must treat '' and 'no_picker' as the same bucket, and that is stated in the runbook rather than left to be discovered.

2. picker_unusable could fire on a shape that is actually fine — e.g. a future step storing its output as a map. Bounded: it is a label on a path that already produced no pages, so no behaviour changes either way; the cost of a mislabel is a wasted look, not a wrong link.

3. This does not add a durable record on the LOAD step's failure, which runs before any model call. That failure still leaves no llm_call_log row and now reports no_picker — which is CORRECT and is the point, but it does not distinguish 'load failed' from 'step unwired'. Stated rather than fixed; the runbook names the signature (skips with no picker calls at all).

4. Inert until a chassis roll, like any Go change here. The council-approved 602 config is already live, so between this commit and the roll the empty-source ambiguity persists exactly as today — no window is opened that was not already open.

5. ROUND 2: the Defaults guard is a source-scanning assertion over a spec literal, so it can only see a Default declared in THAT spec. A default injected elsewhere — a registry wrapper, a future per-step config default — would not be caught. Stated rather than solved; the guard covers the declared surface, which is where every existing Default on this estate lives.
